title: Review of the firefly visual system (Coleoptera: Lampyridae) and evolution of the opsin genes underlying color vision
why: Lampyris: a hit of the harvest's family review "Lampyridae vision review" (no abstract stored). A review of the firefly visual system covers eye types and eye structure across fireflies, so it may give an interommatidial angle (interommatidial_deg) or an acuity (acuity_cpd) for the common glow-worm Lampyris noctiluca, whose males find glowing females by sight; main's one value for the species is an acceptance angle from Booth, Stewart and Osorio 2004 (sweep-53). It is already on main's insect wanted list for receptor classes, eye types and night sensitivity, with the authors named there; no harvest output or search result of this unit shows the authors. The web pair "Lampyris visual acuity" and "glow-worm visual acuity" returned no acuity study of the genus. Not opened.
get: journal via library (closed in the harvest listing)

title: A method for compound eye mapping: Dimensions and regional variations in firefly (Coleoptera: Lampyridae) compound eye
journal: University of Connecticut dissertation (Digital Commons AAI3308226)
why: Lampyris: returned by the web search "Lampyris visual acuity" (title and link only). A dissertation that maps the dimensions and regional variation of firefly compound eyes may give interommatidial angles (interommatidial_deg) and acuities (acuity_cpd) for the species it studied, and the result shows none of them. The same search returned a conference paper on the compound eye of Photinus carolinus, so the dissertation's fireflies are probably North American, and Lampyris does not occur in North America (my own knowledge); a Lampyris species is therefore unlikely among them, and the line is background. The year and author are not shown on the result. Not opened.
get: thesis via ProQuest (AAI3308226) or the UConn Digital Commons record

title: Morphological traits of the eyes of Lepidoptera indicate selection for binocular vision in both diurnal butterflies and nocturnal moths
why: Panopoda and Glenoides, acuity_cpd and interommatidial_deg: an eye-morphology study of 224 butterfly and moth species, as main's wanted lines describe it, whose species table main has not read, so the red-lined panopoda (Panopoda rufimargo, Erebidae) or the Texas gray (Glenoides texanaria, Geometridae) may be among its species, with eye measurements from which an interommatidial angle or an anatomical acuity could follow. The desk holds the Lepidoptera acuity cells of earlier units on the same work (harvest-30 onward). Neither genus's harvest returned it, and the acuity pairs ("Panopoda visual acuity", "red-lined panopoda visual acuity", "Glenoides visual acuity", "Texas gray moth visual acuity") returned no eye measurement for either moth. A title search returned the Pierce laboratory's publication page, a Harvard DASH record and the announcement of Wei-Ping Chan's thesis defence (Naomi Pierce, adviser), and no page showing its DOI, year or authors; main's wanted lines (harvest-30 to -42) cite it as a 2024 Research Square preprint with a DOI, so those fields are left to the registry. Not opened.
get: open preprint (Research Square, per main's wanted lines); the Pierce laboratory page: https://piercelab.oeb.harvard.edu/publication/morphological-traits-eyes-lepidoptera-indicate-selection-binocular-vision-both-diurnal

journal: ESA Annual Meetings Online Program, 2011 (esa.confex.com, paper 58852)
why: Panopoda, acuity_cpd and interommatidial_deg: a 2011 meeting abstract that came up, without a title, for both web searches "Panopoda visual acuity" and "red-lined panopoda visual acuity", so its text may name the genus beside an eye or acuity measure; the same searches also returned a study of the eyes of a sea spider (Pantopoda), so the match may be a near-homonym.
